highest_reported.source_location: §5.1, Table 1, row VT_0(n) code, column n=16; also row Ours (search over s=1)
highest_reported.reproduction_status: The n=16 VT_0 witness is frozen locally and exactly verified. The paper's LLM-guided search rediscovers a priority function proved equivalent to VT_0; it does not establish maximum cardinality at n=16.
highest_reported.ai_provenance: The paper reports an LLM-guided evolutionary rediscovery of the classical VT_0 construction, with a proof of equivalence. It reports the same 3856 size, not a larger code or a finite-n optimality proof.

parameters.decoding_condition: distinct codewords have disjoint sets of length-15 deletion outputs

known_bounds.lower_bound_location: §5.1, Table 1, VT_0(n) code row, n=16 column
known_bounds.upper_bound_location: §5.1, Table 1, LP upper bound row, n=16 column
known_bounds.status: A feasible 3856-word code is known. The paper states that VT_0 is conjectured largest for all finite lengths; optimality is proved only through n=11. Its n=16 LP upper bound is 4202. The exact maximum at n=16 remains open in the sources checked on 2026-11-06.

human_construction.source_location: Varshamov and Tenengolts (1965) introduce the checksum class for single asymmetric-error correction. Levenshtein (1965 original/1966 English translation) establishes its single-deletion-correcting property; the current paper §2.2 states the VT checksum definition.
human_construction.reproduction_status: Generated from the modular checksum formula and checked by the exact pairwise deletion-output checker.

ai_assisted_record.status: The LLM-guided search rediscovers a function proved equivalent to VT_0. This is recorded separately from the classical human construction and does not improve its cardinality or prove the n=16 maximum.

independent_quantity.method: independent string slicing at each deletion index, with per-word duplicates removed
